correctness.rationale: For x in P1 intersect P2 the classical fiber sum is theta I1(x)+(1-theta)I2(x), an interval of length theta*l1(x)+(1-theta)*l2(x); outside the intersection it is empty. Fubini integrates this to area(Ftheta). Subtracting Cavalieri area(Ki)=integral_{Pi} li yields exactly theta*integral_{P1\P2}l1+(1-theta)*integral_{P2\P1}l2. With theta strictly in (0,1), full-dimensional planar bodies have strictly positive fiber lengths in the interior of projection intervals. Distinct compact projection intervals have a positive-length interval in at least one difference, so deficit>0; equal intervals make it zero. Boundary theta=0/1 is correctly excluded. Exact independent checks give (overlap, output, weighted, deficit)=(2,4,6,2) for the nested rectangles and (3/2,5,20/3,5/3) for overlapping unequal projections. Both have origin interior. Finite checks corroborate, and the general proof is the integral argument, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: The source uses a literal ?_{L|M} in one display; the classical fiber operation is nonetheless unambiguous in surrounding prose and proof.
The case of disjoint projections yields empty output, with area interpreted as zero; the actual published counterexample uses origin-containing rectangles.

evidence: The 2025 published Theorem 2.8 prints vol_2(F_theta)^(1/2) >= theta*vol_2(K1)^(1/2) + (1-theta)*vol_2(K2)^(1/2), which is contradicted even more sharply by the rectangles: left 2 vs right (sqrt(4)+sqrt(8))/2 > 2.
The paper also prints the corresponding p=1 case of its general theorem, and its classical fiber sum construction restricts to common projections.
McMullen 1999 was identified as the cited source but full text was unavailable; original hypotheses were not assumed from Hoehner–Xing's paraphrase.
